canonical_jtbd: When I publish a new article on dev.to, I want to automatically republish it to my other platforms (Medium, personal blog, LinkedIn) with correct formatting, so I can save 30-60 minutes per article and ensure consistent cross-posting.

current_workaround: Copy-paste article content, reformat Markdown, re-upload images, and adjust tags for each target platform.

source_evidence.workflow: Manually republishing dev.to articles to other platforms (Medium, personal blog, LinkedIn) one by one without any automation

source_evidence.current_workaround: Copy-paste article content, reformat Markdown, re-upload images, and adjust tags for each target platform

canonical_jtbd: When spam messages bypass Discord's built-in AutoMod, I want to automatically detect and remove them using custom regex filters, so I can protect community trust and reduce moderator workload.
painful_workflow: Manually reviewing and removing spam messages that bypass Discord's built-in AutoMod, using third-party bots or manual deletion.
current_workaround: Use third-party moderation bots with custom regex filters (e.g., Dyno, Carl-bot) or manually delete messages and ban users.

source_evidence.workflow: Manual review and removal of spam messages that bypass Discord's built-in AutoMod (e.g., repeated links, scam messages using character manipulation).

source_evidence.current_workaround: Use third-party moderation bots with custom regex filters (e.g., Dyno, Carl-bot) or manually delete messages and ban users.

canonical_jtbd: When I add new roles or modify permissions in a large Discord server, I want to automatically track role hierarchy and permissions to avoid conflicts, so I can prevent security breaches and data exposure.
painful_workflow: Manually tracking role permissions and hierarchy using spreadsheets to avoid permission conflicts in large multi-community servers.
current_workaround: Maintain a separate spreadsheet mapping roles → permissions → channel overrides, or use a third-party bot that logs permission changes.

source_evidence.workflow: Manual tracking of role permissions and hierarchy using spreadsheets to avoid permission conflicts in large multi-community servers.
source_evidence.trigger: Adding a new role or modifying permissions for existing roles.
source_evidence.current_workaround: Maintain a separate spreadsheet mapping roles → permissions → channel overrides, or use a third-party bot that logs permission changes.
source_evidence.consequence: Permission errors can lead to security breaches or accidental data exposure; manual spreadsheet updates are error-prone and not real-time.

canonical_jtbd: When I restructure my Discord server or fear accidental deletion, I want to automatically back up server configuration and message history, so I can avoid hours of recreation and data loss.
painful_workflow: Manually backing up server configuration (roles, channels, permissions) and message history using third-party tools or bots.
current_workaround: Use bots like DiscordChatExporter for message backups, and manually copy role/channel settings via screenshots or text files.

source_evidence.workflow: Manual backup of server configuration (roles, channels, permissions) and message history by exporting data via third-party tools or bots.
source_evidence.trigger: Server restructuring, fear of accidental deletion, or migration to a new server.
source_evidence.current_workaround: Use bots like DiscordChatExporter for message backups, and manually copy role/channel settings via screenshots or text files.
source_evidence.consequence: Without a backup, accidental deletion of a channel or role set can take hours to recreate; manual backups are rarely comprehensive and often neglected.
